# hetznerrobot_firewall (Resource)

The complete Robot firewall of one dedicated server — status, flags and every input and output rule. Each apply sends the whole configuration and waits until Robot has applied it. Either configure the rules here or apply a `template_id`; whatever is left out keeps the value Robot holds — adopting a firewall without listing its rules keeps them. Destroying the resource clears the firewall configuration.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "hetznerrobot_firewall" "web" {
  server_number = 321
  filter_ipv6   = true

  input_rules = [
    { name = "ssh from office", ip_version = "ipv4", src_ip = "198.51.100.0/24", dst_port = "22", protocol = "tcp", action = "accept" },
    { name = "https", dst_port = "443", action = "accept" },
    { name = "replies", ip_version = "ipv4", dst_port = "32768-65535", protocol = "tcp", tcp_flags = "ack", action = "accept" },
    { name = "drop the rest", action = "discard" },
  ]
  output_rules = [
    { name = "allow all", action = "accept" },
  ]
}

# Or apply a template instead of listing the rules.
resource "hetznerrobot_firewall" "db" {
  server_number = 421
  template_id   = hetznerrobot_firewall_template.base.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `server_number` (Number) Server the firewall belongs to.

### Optional

- `filter_ipv6` (Boolean) Whether IPv6 traffic is filtered too.
- `input_rules` (Attributes List) Rules for incoming packets, matched in order. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--input_rules))
- `output_rules` (Attributes List) Rules for outgoing packets, matched in order. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--output_rules))
- `status` (String) `active` or `disabled`. Left out, it becomes `active` when rules or a template are configured and keeps the live status otherwise.
- `template_id` (Number) Firewall template to apply. It is applied when it is set or changed — later edits of the template do not reach this server until the template is applied again. Conflicts with the rules and `whitelist_hos`.
- `whitelist_hos` (Boolean) Whether Hetzner services (rescue, DHCP, …) are always let through. Left out, it keeps the live value.

### Read-Only

- `port` (String) Switch port the firewall sits on (`main` or `kvm`).
- `server_ip` (String) Main IP address of the server.

<a id="nestedatt--input_rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `input_rules`

Required:

- `action` (String) `accept` or `discard`.

Optional:

- `dst_ip` (String) Destination address or subnet in CIDR notation (IPv4 rules only).
- `dst_port` (String) Destination port or range, e.g. `80` or `32768-65535`.
- `ip_version` (String) `ipv4` or `ipv6`; left out, the rule matches both.
- `name` (String) Name of the rule.
- `protocol` (String) `tcp`, `udp`, `gre`, `icmp`, `ipip`, `ah` or `esp`; needs `ip_version`.
- `src_ip` (String) Source address or subnet in CIDR notation (IPv4 rules only).
- `src_port` (String) Source port or range.
- `tcp_flags` (String) TCP flag or logical combination of flags, e.g. `syn` or `syn|ack`.


<a id="nestedatt--output_rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `output_rules`

Required:

- `action` (String) `accept` or `discard`.

Optional:

- `dst_ip` (String) Destination address or subnet in CIDR notation (IPv4 rules only).
- `dst_port` (String) Destination port or range, e.g. `80` or `32768-65535`.
- `ip_version` (String) `ipv4` or `ipv6`; left out, the rule matches both.
- `name` (String) Name of the rule.
- `protocol` (String) `tcp`, `udp`, `gre`, `icmp`, `ipip`, `ah` or `esp`; needs `ip_version`.
- `src_ip` (String) Source address or subnet in CIDR notation (IPv4 rules only).
- `src_port` (String) Source port or range.
- `tcp_flags` (String) TCP flag or logical combination of flags, e.g. `syn` or `syn|ack`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
tofu import hetznerrobot_firewall.web 321
```
